claims.statement: A numerical trajectory in the six-site cospherical example crosses the active facet at about model time 0.748, despite a common unique attracting equilibrium.
claims.limitations: Constructed example at beta=1.2; time is in model units.

claims.statement: A fixed equal-mass one-prototype readout is equivalent to choosing the nearest prototype; transport and score evaluation are distinct operations.
claims.limitations: Nearest-site depiction uses one prototype per class and equal masses.

claims.statement: Delivery territories, currents and carousel are visual analogies; a full rotation illustrates one possible return with intervening crossings.
claims.limitations: Analogy. The rotor does not satisfy the Gaussian gradient-flow hypotheses.

claims.statement: Equal-mass rectangle vertices have invariant affine decision cells because each exposed facet plane reflects the prototype set.
claims.limitations: Exact geometric example; unique common attractor in the depicted rectangle at beta=2.

claims.statement: Normal velocity is a weighted average of projection-group normal means; every group must balance on each facet for global invariance.
claims.limitations: Shared spherical Gaussian model and affine strict decision cells. Pairs are a sufficient example of balance.

claims.statement: Preserving all strict decisions at one fixed positive horizon is equivalent to preservation at all horizons. If balances fail, an open set switches at each horizon.
claims.limitations: No claim about how many switch under a particular feature law, or which points recur.

claims.statement: With precision diag(2,1) and equal sites ±(1,1), the Euclidean gradient has normal drift on 2x+y=0, while the preconditioned field preserves the plane.
claims.limitations: Two explicitly different fields with the same fixed readout.

claims.statement: A reachable tangential projection and a worst-case normal velocity certify sufficient distance for whole-interval preservation; unsupported queries are unresolved by the guard.
claims.limitations: Exact-arithmetic conditions for the spherical model, evaluated numerically in the learned data study.

claims.statement: At T=0.50 and standard deviation/diameter=0.35, covariance versus local guard coverage was 93.29% versus 96.64% (Iris), 14.75% versus 65.06% (Letter), 30.32% versus 86.23% (HAR).
claims.limitations: Fixed descriptive cohorts of 149, 3620 and 864 rows/windows; HAR uses nine held-out subjects; coverage is not ground-truth accuracy.

claims.statement: Across 51 exact fixture query/horizon combinations the terminal label was always resolved; 41 same, 10 changed. Whole-path status resolved 29 preserve, 10 depart, 12 unresolved.
claims.limitations: Two fixed two-dimensional fixtures, 17 points at three horizons. Counts are combinations, not 51 independent trajectories.

claims.statement: First test fold median hybrid relative to full RK4: Iris 1.04×, Letter 2.03×, HAR 0.34×.
claims.limitations: One machine and thread, setup excluded, batch cap 64, matched RK4 maximum step 0.1, ratio of medians.

claims.statement: Synthetic K=3 ratio 0.145–0.697, K=40 ratio 1.33–2.46 with 77–100% local coverage.
claims.limitations: One measured host and workload; two dimensions, two overlap settings, three seeds; no general speed guarantee.

claims.statement: The predicted decision and its correctness under the external label law are distinct. A structural certificate is about the former.
claims.limitations: Class accuracy requires true labels; no universal accuracy or acceleration gain.
